I compared the 100 measured edits for pairs of parents that differ mainly in one condition. Ten interactions recur across C10, C100 and IN16. Some rest on only one or two matched pairs, so they are well supported directionally but not proven.

**Pattern 1: no direct path from input to output (edge 3 = `none`).** Without that path, the cell has no shortcut from input to output. Edits that add or strengthen any path then gain much more, on all three datasets, than the same edits on a parent with edge 3 = `skip_connect`.

| Edit | Edge 3 = `none` (exp. #) | Edge 3 = `skip_connect` (exp. #) |
|---|---|---|
| Edge 3 → `skip_connect` (edge 3 not already skip) | #13, 21, 22, 23: up to +3.9 / +8.0 / +17.3 | edge 3 already a conv or pool, #14–16: smaller gains, e.g. #15 is −1.19 / +0.87 / +0.95 |
| Edge 3 → `nor_conv_3x3` | #84: +3.5 / +7.1 / +16.7 | #83: +1.6 / −0.7 / +5.5 |
| Edge 5 → `nor_conv_3x3` | #82: +2.5 / +7.2 / +15.4 | #81: +1.2 / +2.9 / +6.5 |
| Edge 0 → `nor_conv_3x3` | #35: +3.2 / +7.7 / +6.9 | #25: +0.4 / +3.2 / +1.3 |
| Edge 4 → `skip_connect` | #64: all three positive | #63: mixed |
| Edge 1 → `skip_connect` | #68: all three positive | #67: mostly negative |
| Edge 5 → `skip_connect` | #60: all three positive | #59: mostly negative |

**Pattern 2: edges 4 and 5 back each other up.**
* Adding `nor_conv_3x3` on edge 4 gains much more when edge 5 = `none` (#38: +4.9 / +13.4 / +16.9) than when edge 5 carries a conv (#37).
* Removing edge 5 hurts far more when edge 4 = `none` (#70, IN16 −16.3) than when edge 4 is a conv (#69).
* Removing edge 4 hurts far more when edge 5 = `none` (#73) than when edge 5 is a conv (#72).
